wa_dragontail_peak_backbone_ridge.notes: From the top of the 4th-class approach ledges, climb the low-angle white corner to the ridge crest, then follow the crest up to a stance at the foot of the obvious offwidth. Belay on the ledge below the wide crack.

The crux offwidth, straight up. The lower half takes small and hand-sized cams; the upper half protects only with a very large cam (BD #6), bumped along as you go. Some parties get by with a #5 and runout. Packs make it much harder, so haul or hang them. Expect a strenuous, knee-and-ankle-scraping struggle. Belay on hand-sized gear above.

Walk left from the belay and climb a long, blocky open-book corner toward a small roof. Short of the roof, step right and build the belay. Protection is good in the corner cracks; small cams and offset nuts are useful at the anchor.

Climb a low-angle finger crack just left of the crest; when it widens, step left into a wide-hands layback. From the top of the layback, trend left through cracks and blocks to the sharp ridgeline. The move off the finger crack is the pitch's crux and relies on small edges or smears.

Step down and left from the sharp ridge onto a large ledge, then scramble back to the crest and follow it to a small saddle below the Fin. The rock is lichen-covered and loose in places, with several possible lines; most parties simul-climb this section, keeping to the left side of the ridge where the choice is unclear. Watch rope drag and loose blocks.
Take the ramp up toward the base of the Fin headwall, crossing a gravel apron, and belay on a left-leaning ledge below the twin cracks. Easy ground, but gravel on the ledges makes it slick underfoot.

The first Fin pitch: climb the twin cracks and face holds above the ledge to a large flat ledge. Gear spacing is reasonable; a grassy crack to the right is an alternative but dirtier. Loose blocks sit on the ledge at the top, so place a high directional to keep the rope from pulling them onto the second.

The hardest Fin pitch: a tricky hand and finger crack around the left corner of the arête, then a right-facing corner to a semi-hanging stance straddling the Fin crest below a large roof. Superb rock in an exposed position. Ledge-fall potential low on the pitch; protect it well. The belay takes #1–#3 cams.

Climb the blocky crack a short way, then traverse right along horizontal cracks across the face of the Fin: a long, rising, near-horizontal shuffle past the roof with poor feet, few holds and very exposed. Gear is sparse in the middle, so protect well for the second as well as the leader. Some rock near the end of the traverse is questionable. Belay at the notch between gendarmes.

Easy but loose terrain along ledges and gravelly gullies toward the summit; most parties simul-climb or short-rope it. Choose flake anchors carefully and manage drag around the small walls. Near the top, a gravel apron and a shallow gully lead up and left to the summit, or contour left sooner to join the descent trail.

wa_flycatcher_buttress.notes: Head mostly straight up the natural features. The climbing is straightforward, but good gear placements are harder to find than the angle suggests. Belay at a slung tree, or continue to the next ledge above.

Downclimb to below the steep face, then traverse hard right for a full rope-length. Several ledges at the end of the traverse offer a belay; protect the follower as well as the leader on this sideways ground.
Mostly walking with a little easy climbing, heading to the right side of a big ledge.
Step right and make an awkward step up into a slabby corner. Build a solid anchor near the chimney, or continue left to a large ledge instead.
Several lines are possible. A good choice is a low-angle hand crack that leads to a big ledge right below the crux pitch.
The crux pitch. Where the wall shows a pair of cracks, take the left one.
Climb mostly straight up to a good ledge.
Traverse left to an exposed, wider crack. Do not go straight up off the belay, which is the easy mistake to make here.
Choose a variation: climb cracks and make an awkward step left to reach a hand crack, or take the squeeze chimney. A #5 cam is useful on the wide options.
Easy climbing to the summit plateau. To descend, cross to the west side of the peak for the rappels.
